title: Release-candidate check — catalogue search, sorting and category filter
context: Release-candidate re-check of the catalogue search, sorting, category filter and pagination criteria (stated as the same as TOOL-1), run on the release-candidate environment before promotion. The web shop and the public catalogue API used by the mobile app must behave the same way.

sourcesRead.contributes: all criteria (L25-L31), API endpoints and response shape (L21), category lookup (L35), scope (L19, L36)

acceptanceCriteria.text: Searching the web shop for a term shows only products whose name contains the term, and a caption "Searched for: <term>".
acceptanceCriteria.quote: Searching the web shop for a term shows only products whose name contains the term, and a caption "Searched for: <term>".
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: web shop catalogue home page on the release-candidate environment (G1); search control per G2
outcomes: every product shown has a name that contains the term (matched regardless of letter case, per G7)
caption "Searched for: <term>" is shown with the searched term

acceptanceCriteria.text: GET /products/search?q=<term> returns 200 with only products whose name contains the term, regardless of letter case (searching "PLIERS" finds the same products as "pliers").
acceptanceCriteria.quote: GET /products/search?q=<term> returns 200 with only products whose name contains the term, regardless of letter case (searching "PLIERS" finds the same products as "pliers").
outcomes: every product in data has a name that contains the term, ignoring letter case
searching "PLIERS" finds the same products as "pliers"

acceptanceCriteria.text: A search without matches shows "There are no products found." on the web shop, and the API returns 200 with an empty data list and total 0.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: A search without matches shows "There are no products found." on the web shop, and the API returns 200 with an empty data list and total 0.
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: web shop catalogue home page on the release-candidate environment (G1); search control per G2
outcomes: web shop shows "There are no products found."
API data is an empty list

acceptanceCriteria.text: Choosing "Price (Low - High)" on the web shop lists the products by ascending price; GET /products?sort=price,asc returns the products in ascending price order.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: Choosing "Price (Low - High)" on the web shop lists the products by ascending price; GET /products?sort=price,asc returns the products in ascending price order.
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: web shop catalogue home page on the release-candidate environment (G1); sort control per G2
outcomes: after choosing "Price (Low - High)" the web shop lists the products by ascending price
GET /products?sort=price,asc returns the products in ascending price order

acceptanceCriteria.text: Filtering the web shop by the category "Hammer" shows only hammers; GET /products?by_category=<id of Hammer> returns only products in that category.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: Filtering the web shop by the category "Hammer" shows only hammers; GET /products?by_category=<id of Hammer> returns only products in that category.
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: web shop catalogue home page on the release-candidate environment (G1); category filter per G2
outcomes: after filtering the web shop by the category "Hammer" only hammers are shown
GET /products?by_category=<id of Hammer> returns only products in the category "Hammer"

acceptanceCriteria.text: Results are paginated with 12 products per page (per_page 12) on the web shop and in the API.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: Results are paginated with 12 products per page (per_page 12) on the web shop and in the API.
acceptanceCriteria.entryPoint: web shop catalogue home page on the release-candidate environment (G1); pagination per G2
outcomes: an API page holds at most 12 products in data, and exactly 12 when it is not the last page
a web shop results page shows at most 12 products, and exactly 12 when it is not the last page

acceptanceCriteria.text: An empty search (no term) returns all products, so the mobile app can reuse the search endpoint for its "All tools" screen.
acceptanceCriteria.quote: An empty search (no term) returns all products, so the mobile app can reuse the search endpoint for its "All tools" screen.
outcomes: an empty search on the search endpoint returns all products: its total equals the total of GET /products without filters

endpoints.request: query parameters sort (e.g. sort=price,asc) and by_category (a category id); paginated
none; used to look up the id of the category named Hammer

rules.text: The web shop and the public catalogue API (used by our mobile app) must behave the same way.
GET /products and GET /products/search both return { "current_page", "data": [products], "per_page", "total", "last_page" }; GET /products is paginated.

auth.mechanism: none: the story calls it the public catalogue API

testData.strategy: none needed: read-only checks against the existing catalogue of the release-candidate environment
constraints: search terms PLIERS / pliers for the case-insensitivity check (story.md#L26)
a search term that matches no product for AC-3 (story.md#L27), chosen by the evaluator, e.g. a random string
the category Hammer, whose id is looked up in GET /categories/tree (story.md#L29, story.md#L35)
